articles.body: A feature factory ships a lot and learns little. Ten warning signs, a scorecard you can run in five minutes, and the changes that move a team from output to outcomes. A feature factory is a product team that measures success by how much it ships rather than by whether the work changed anything for customers or the business. John Cutler named the pattern in 2016. The ten warning signs below cover culture, process and follow-through. If four or more describe your team, you are probably shipping without evidence. Key takeaways John Cutler's 2016 post listed 12 signs of a feature factory, starting with "no measurement" and "celebrating launches" ( Cutler, 2016 ).

articles.title: Everything your AI can do with a computer of its own: a WBX Sandbox feature tour
articles.excerpt: Isolated Linux microVMs in the EU, for AI assistants without code and for agents you build yourself. AI assistants are good at writing code. Running it is a different story. The assistant can't instal…
articles.body: Isolated Linux microVMs in the EU, for AI assistants without code and for agents you build yourself. AI assistants are good at writing code. Running it is a different story. The assistant can't install packages on your computer, it shouldn't touch your files, and a chat window is a poor place for a two-hour job. WBX Sandbox gives the AI its own isolated computer in the EU. It installs what it needs, runs the code, and hands back the result: a file, a chart, a link, a test report. Nothing runs on your machine. This post is a tour of what the platform does, so you can picture what to build with it: what you get if you just connect your assistant, and what's there when you write your own agents. Two ways in Without code: connect your AI assistant once.

articles.title: RICE Framework with AI: Score Features on Evidence, Not Guesses
articles.excerpt: AI doesn't change the RICE formula. It changes where the inputs come from. Here is the formula, a worked example and a four-step workflow for scoring Reach, Impact, Confidence and Effort from evidence…
articles.body: AI doesn't change the RICE formula. It changes where the inputs come from. Here is the formula, a worked example and a four-step workflow for scoring Reach, Impact, Confidence and Effort from evidence. The RICE framework scores a piece of work as (Reach × Impact × Confidence) ÷ Effort. Intercom built it and Sean McBride published it in 2018. AI does not change the formula; it changes where the inputs come from. Used well, AI pulls Reach from usage data, Impact from clustered customer feedback and Confidence from the evidence you actually hold, so the score stops being a dressed-up guess. Key takeaways RICE uses fixed scales: Impact runs 0.25 to 3, Confidence is 100%, 80% or 50%, and Effort is in person-months ( Intercom, 2018 ). The weakest inputs are Impact and Effort.

articles.title: 37.1 MiB/s with Zero Token Overflows: Guaranteed Token Budgets and Table-Aware Chunking in text-chipper
articles.excerpt: In RAG pipelines, text chunking usually forces an uncomfortable trade-off: Fast window splitters (like a raw tiktoken loop) are quick, but they slice right through Markdown code blocks, split words in…
articles.body: In RAG pipelines, text chunking usually forces an uncomfortable trade-off: Fast window splitters (like a raw tiktoken loop) are quick, but they slice right through Markdown code blocks, split words in half, and orphan table rows from their column headers. Structure-aware splitters try to respect document layout, but they are often 4×–11× slower, pull in dozens of dependencies, and frequently overshoot hard token limits (returning 513–514 tokens on a 512-token budget when headings or BPE boundary joins aren't re-counted). With text-chipper v1.1.0 , the goal was to eliminate that trade-off: build the fastest chunker that guarantees both strict token budgets and Markdown/table structural awareness , backed by reproducible benchmarks.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of lightwhile observing Jupiter and its moon volcanic moon Io. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

articles.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026.
